propositions: The parameter force_close_reason is declared in transition_core but never referenced in the function body, causing operator-supplied --force=<reason> values to be silently discarded

The force_close_reason value is supplied by the caller at transition_close.py:474 but never written to the durable STATUS event, only optionally recorded in a second lock acquisition that can fail under contention

The fix writes force_close_reason into the close STATUS event as a present-only field mirroring close_class, ensuring it survives in reduced state and is never lost on concurrent close or lock timeout
A close without --force must omit the reason key entirely to remain byte-identical to pre-change events for backward compatibility with older readers
